title: LungEEO: AnOptimized Explainable Ensemble Framework for Lung Cancer Prediction
content: Lung cancer remains one of the leading causes of cancer-related mortality worldwide, highlighting the importance of early detection for improving patient survival rates. However, current machine learning approaches for lung cancer prediction often depend on suboptimal model configurations, limited systematic ensemble comparisons, and insufficient interpretability. This study introduces a novel framework, called Lung Explainable Ensemble Optimizer (LungEEO), that integrates three methodological advances: (1) comprehensive hyperparameter optimization across 74 configurations of twelve machine learning algorithms for base model selection, (2) a systematic comparison of four ensemble strategies—unweighted hard voting, weighted hard voting, soft voting, and stacking—against the best single model under nested cross-validation, and (3) a dual explainable AI (XAI) layer based on SHAP and LIME to provide parallel global and local explanations. To make sure the reported differences reflect genuine effects rather than sampling noise, every ensemble-versus-single-model comparison is backed by a small suite of statistical analyses: repeated cross-validation estimates of stability, paired bootstrap confidence intervals (1,000 resamples) on the AUC differences, exact McNemar tests on the paired predictions, and calibration checks using Brier scores and expected calibration error. Experiments on two heterogeneous lung cancer datasets (5,000 survey records and 20,000 synthetic records) demonstrate that ensemble methods cannot compensate for limited predictive signal. On Dataset 1, logistic regression achieves the highest AUC (0.9254), while ensembles achieve higher accuracy (0.902–0.904). On Dataset 2, all models perform near chance (AUC: 0.479–0.521), with high accuracy driven by class imbalance (86.92%). Integrating SHAP and LIME provides complementary global and local interpretability. Overall, LungEEO offers a reproducible, leakage-free framework balancing predictive performance and interpretability while transparently reporting both positive and null results.
